questiontext.text:
{@word_3@} letters are chosen at random from the word {@word1@}. Find the probability that {@word_4@} letters chosen are consonants.

Note: Give your answer as a fraction

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

If \(S\) is the probability space, then \( \displaystyle n(S)=^{@wordlength1@}C_{@word_1@}=\frac{{@wordlength1@}!}{{@word_1@}!({@wordlength1@}-{@word_1@})!}={@ta_1@}\) .

Let \(E\) be the event “{@word_3@} consonants are chosen”. Since there are {@word_4@} consonants, then \(\displaystyle ^{@word_2@}C_{@word_1@}={@ta_2@}.\)

Therefore \(\displaystyle P(E)=\frac{n(E)}{n(S)}=\frac{{@ta_2@}}{{@ta_1@}}={@ta@}\)

questionnote.text: {@word_3@} letters are chosen at random from the word {@word1@}. The probability that all {@word_3@} letters chosen are consonants is \({@ta@}\).
